def: A foundation model used to judge which tasks or states are interesting, standing in for human taste when a system chooses what to explore next.
Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness: a curriculum that combines learning progress with a language model's judgement of which tasks are worth learning.
An extension of OMNI in which language models also write the code for new environments, rewards and success checks.
How quickly an agent's success rate on a task is changing, used to find tasks that are learnable right now.
A task the agent can currently improve on, neither impossible for it nor already mastered.
A task that is only a minor change to one the agent has already learned, such as the same job with a different number.
A store of every task tried, with its description, code and whether it was learned or failed, used to propose and filter new tasks.
A check that rejects a proposed task if it is too similar to tasks already in the archive.
A program, often written by a model, that decides whether an agent has completed a generated task.
A hard-exploration method that uses a foundation model to judge which states are interesting enough to archive and return to.
The risk that once a generator is optimised against a judge's scores, those scores stop reflecting what people actually find interesting.
